creator: Alexander Terp
description:
MIP-1. muster_dispatch(request_bytes) -> response_bytes over a C ABI, with Muster's vocabulary defined in .proto and generated on both sides, so a vocabulary change is one edit rather than two that drift.

The part MIP-1 flags as most likely to be got wrong, and which protobuf does not solve: the push direction. The core has to wake the shell unasked - an agent changed state, a daemon event landed, a notification is due - which is a registered callback pointer or a channel the shell drains. Backpressure when the shell is slow to drain has no design yet.

The same schema is the CLI and agent-facing API surface, so 'one action path, parity by construction' becomes codegen rather than discipline.
title: The shell/core seam: one symbol, protobuf, and a way to push
